stem:
A fixed mass of an ideal gas has a volume *V* and a pressure *p*.

The gas undergoes a cycle of changes, X to Y to Z to X, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Table 2.1 shows data for *p*, *V* and temperature *T* for the gas at points X, Y and Z.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the change in internal energy Δ*U* for one complete cycle, XYZX.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Complete Table 2.1.
Use the space below for any working.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
The first law of thermodynamics for a system may be represented by the equation

Δ*U* = *q* + *W*.

State, with reference to the system, what is meant by:

Δ*U*:

*q*:

*W*:

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how the first law of thermodynamics applies to the change Z to X.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A pressure–volume graph showing the cycle X to Y to Z to X, with a curved path from Z to X and vertical and horizontal paths between Y and Z and between X and Y.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for p / 10⁵ Pa, V / 10⁻³ m³ and T / K, and rows X, Y and Z; the printed values are X: 1.5, 4.2, 540; Y: temperature 230; Z: 5.1, temperature 782, with the remaining cells blank.
